clue.text: Beaming American girl selecting the actors

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman or girl
casting is the choosing of actors for parts in a play or film

explanation.surface: A young American woman, all smiles, choosing the cast for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaming' looks like a description of the happy girl, but it is the definition in its radio sense of sending out a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam a programme is to transmit it over the airwaves, which is what radio and television stations do.

clue.text: Dog in abject state, originally, I found

parts.note: abject and base both mean low and contemptible
NJ, New Jersey, was one of the thirteen original states of the USA
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog found in a wretched condition by the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' does not pick a first letter: it points to New Jersey as one of the original thirteen American states, abbreviated NJ.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a barkless hunting breed from central Africa.

clue.text: Man at Worcester, perhaps, from Royalists' HQ

explanation.surface: A Worcester man who hails from the King's wartime base.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcester here is an Oxford college, not the city; Oxford was the Royalist headquarters in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxonian is a member of Oxford University, such as a Worcester College man, and also anyone from Oxford, King Charles I's wartime capital.

clue.text: One tried to protect soldier, say

parts.note: to defend something is to protect it
a soldier is one caste of ant, so the insect stands for it

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to shield a soldier, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tried' suggests attempting, but 'One tried' means a person put on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The accused party in a court case is the person whose guilt is being tried.

clue.text: Surrounded by a large number of Romans on galley's prow

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
taken as written

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a ship, so the front letter of the word galley is taken

explanation.surface: Encircled by a crowd of Romans at the front of a galley.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'large number of Romans' sounds like a crowd but is the Roman numeral M.
explanation.definitionFit: Among means in the midst of, enclosed by others.

clue.text: Shoe needed by racehorse

explanation.surface: A racehorse requires a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a horseshoe, but one sense is a sports shoe and the other is the person who prepares a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a sports shoe, and also the person who conditions racehorses for their races.

clue.text: River spirit raised in this state

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are written upwards, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A river spirit is summoned up in a particular country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AIRE plus GIN as a whole, giving NIGER then IA; the River Niger itself is not in the wordplay, though it flows through the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a West African country, a state in the sense of a nation.

clue.text: Measure in support of country police force

indicators.note: in a down clue the measure sits below the country, holding it up

parts.note: Scotland is a country of the UK
a yard is a measure of length

explanation.surface: Taking steps to back the nation's police.
explanation.walkthrough: London's Metropolitan Police headquarters is known as Scotland Yard, so the name stands for the force.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland Yard is the familiar name for the Metropolitan Police, taken from its headquarters.

clue.text: Sail away and leave the Needles behind?

explanation.surface: A yacht sets off and leaves the Isle of Wight's rocks astern.
explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are chalk rocks off the Isle of Wight, but here they are knitting needles: to cast off is to finish the work and take it off them.
explanation.definitionFit: Untying a boat's mooring ropes to depart, and finishing knitting by removing stitches, are both the same phrase.

clue.text: Prokofiev's beloved fruit

parts.note: Prokofiev wrote an opera called The Love for Three of these citrus fruits

explanation.surface: The composer's favourite fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Prokofiev's opera The Love for Three Oranges gives the fruit he 'loved'.
explanation.definitionFit: The opera's title names the citrus fruit the prince falls for, so it is the fruit Prokofiev made beloved.

clue.text: Alternative plan supports place in Herts

parts.note: to second a proposal is to support it
Tring is a town in Hertfordshire, the county north of London

explanation.surface: A backup scheme in favour of somewhere in Hertfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' is the verb seconds, as when someone seconds a motion at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A second string is a fallback option kept in reserve, like an archer's spare bowstring.

clue.text: One isn't loose, showing this

indicators.note: the letters of the words one isn't are let loose and reassembled

explanation.surface: Something that is not slack displays this quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: something that is not loose is taut.
explanation.definitionFit: Tautness is the state of being stretched tight, the opposite of slack.

clue.text: All-encompassing information boy collected

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Comprehensive facts gathered by a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN, short for general information, is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means covering a whole class rather than a particular case.

clue.text: Like crane, say, one mounted in a vehicle

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed up inside the vehicle as a passenger would be

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Similar to a crane, for instance, one loaded onto a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crane' suggests the lifting machine on a truck, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A crane is a bird, and avian means relating to birds.

clue.text: Make sure disorder can't arise

indicators.note: disorder tells us the letters of can't arise are jumbled

explanation.surface: Check that no chaos can break out.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish something for certain is to verify it.

clue.text: Artist producing studies on panel

indicators.note: in a down clue the studies sit on top of the panel

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a table can be a flat panel or slab

explanation.surface: A painter working up sketches on a wooden board.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was the English landscape painter; artists often painted on panels, which deepens the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was a celebrated English landscape painter.

clue.text: Old-fashioned menswear on King and Knave of Hearts, say

definitions.text: King and Knave of Hearts, say

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor times
taken as written

explanation.surface: Period costume worn by playing-card royals.
explanation.walkthrough: Card figures wear doublets, but in bridge two cards held alone in a suit, such as K and J of hearts, form a holding of exactly two.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, a holding of just two cards in a suit has this name, such as King and Jack alone.

clue.text: Disturbances in university circles

parts.note: up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford
turns and circles are both rotations

explanation.surface: Unrest in academic quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for 'in university' is a British usage: students go up to university and come down at the end of term.
explanation.definitionFit: Upturns are upheavals, upsets that overturn things.

clue.text: Desire to fiddle with weapon

parts.note: to long for something is to desire it
to bow is to play a fiddle with a bow

explanation.surface: A wish to tinker with a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like tinkering but means playing a violin, which a musician does with a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: The English longbow was a tall bow used in medieval warfare.

clue.text: Cooking vessels containing blackbirds?

parts.note: kitchen dishes such as a pie would be baked in, recalling the nursery rhyme with four and twenty blackbirds baked in a pie

explanation.surface: Pots holding birds, as in the nursery rhyme pie.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the nursery rhyme Sing a Song of Sixpence, whose pie held blackbirds; such a pie is made in a deep dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep round dishes used in the kitchen for mixing and baking are a familiar kind of cooking vessel.

clue.text: Might she need help with froth on top?

definitions.text: Might she need help with froth on top?

parts.words: Might she need help with froth on top?
parts.note: a woman serving drinks pulls pints that must have a head of foam

explanation.surface: Does a woman need assistance with her frothy top layer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'help' reads as assistance, but the woman serving drinks is herself the help, and the froth is the head on a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman working behind a pub counter pulls pints, which should come with a foamy head.

clue.text: Irish beat disheartened enemy

parts.note: to whisk eggs is to beat them

indicators.note: the heart of the word enemy is removed, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An Irishman thrashed a dispirited foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish' is a noun here: the spirit distilled in Ireland, spelt with an E, unlike Scotch.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish is a name for the spirit distilled in Ireland, as Scotch is for Scotland's.

clue.text: Articles about fashion I needed for girl

indicators.note: the two articles are placed around the remaining pieces

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a is the other form of the indefinite article
ton is fashion or style, from the French
taken as written

explanation.surface: Newspaper features on style that a young woman needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper pieces but means the grammatical words an and a.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonia is a woman's first name.

clue.text: A point in the lead

parts.note: taken as written
a head is a point of land, a headland

explanation.surface: A single score puts a team in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' suggests a score in a game, but it is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front of rivals means leading the race.

clue.text: Dog-fighter? Not on a regular basis

definitions.text: Dog-fighter? Not on a regular basis

parts.words: Dog-fighter? Not on a regular basis
parts.note: a breed of dog that shares its name with a part-time soldier of the Territorial Army, who is not a Regular

explanation.surface: An occasional brawler among dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: A Territorial Army volunteer, a British part-time reservist, is nicknamed by the dog breed's name; Regulars are full-time soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small hunting dog and also a member of Britain's part-time Territorial Army.

clue.text: Bad rule stupidly made permanent

indicators.note: stupidly signals that the letters of bad rule are mixed up

explanation.surface: A foolish regulation was made to last for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long-lasting and hard-wearing is lasting rather than temporary.

clue.text: To run down jet like this is, hardly possible

definitions.text: jet like this is, hardly possible

explanation.surface: Disparaging an aircraft is barely feasible.
explanation.walkthrough: Jet is the glossy black stone, already as dark as can be, so making it darker is hardly possible; the surface suggests an aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: To defame someone is to darken their name, and making something darker is what you cannot do to jet-black stone.

clue.text: Poetical work that starts fast

explanation.surface: A poem that opens at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' reads as quick but is a period of abstaining: Lent, which begins on this day; T. S. Eliot wrote a poem of the same title.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot's 1930 poem has this title, and the day is the first of Lent, the Christian fasting season.
